sections.label: The opening
sections.line: A reply to Florent Daudens: open to agents, paid at the source, and what is still open.
sections.para: Florent Daudens reviewed five publishers' bets for the AI era and concluded that a connector is not a business model. This newsroom separates access from value by design: open CC BY structure for agents, a pay-after-you-read meter for people. It does both directions, to the assistant and into the page, and goes further with vaults that carry identity, permissions and terms, and provenance that travels. Discovery and payment at scale remain open.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: His question, his answer, our separation, both directions, two steps further, and two gaps.
sections.para: Discovery and evidence that people pay are open here as they are for him.

sections.label: His five bets
sections.line: CNA's paid connector, Spiegel's archive in Claude, Every, Axios Direct and State Affairs.
sections.para: CNA launched on 31 August 2026 at NT$200 a month; Spiegel's connector is in Claude's directory; Axios Direct serves Pro Deals subscribers' agents. All ask how to make money if nobody comes to the website.

sections.label: Where we agree: access is not value
sections.line: Accessible to agents is not the same as worth paying for, and this newsroom is built on that.
sections.para: Free and open: markdown twins, graphs, section summaries, llms.txt and a reader API, under CC BY. Paid: the experience at the source, through a meter with £5 of credit, a few pence a read, a price the reader sets, and a balance that can go negative.

sections.label: Both directions, not one
sections.line: We bring the archive to the assistant and the assistant into the page.
sections.para: No MCP connector yet, though the structure is published. In the page, a vault app carries its own model, held to a behaviour policy: Spiegel's choice of what to give the chatbot, written down and enforced.

sections.label: Where we go further, one: the vault as the unit
sections.line: For an Apple News for AI, a shared format rather than a shared platform: the vault.
sections.para: A vault can carry a newsroom's identity in signed commits and tags, permissions denied by default, and its licence and price, so a reader app could open many newsrooms' vaults. Proposed, not built for many newsrooms.

sections.label: Where we go further, two: provenance travels
sections.line: Provenance travels: sources, checked quotes, stale-checked summaries, versions and signed commits.
sections.para: An answer citing a section by anchor can be checked against the exact version. After connection, readers tell the newsroom what they needed with the Pen, and keep their own state in their own vault.

sections.label: What is still open, here too
sections.line: Discovery, whether people pay at scale, and agents paying per use are still open here.
sections.para: llms.txt does not make an assistant recommend you; the meter is a small experiment; per-use payment by agents is proposed.

sections.label: What this does not claim
sections.line: Publishers as described in his essay, partly checked; no MCP connector; the shared format is proposed.
sections.para: The meter's results are not published here.

sections.label: Where this comes from
sections.line: His LinkedIn post and Substack essay, Focus Taiwan, Claude's directory, Digiday, and earlier replies here.
